title: Safely managed drinking water, SDG regions compared
headline: Central and Southern Asia: safely managed drinking water up 29.2 points since 2000
subtitle: Proportion of the population using drinking water from an improved source that is accessible on premises, available when needed and free from contamination
years: Central and S. Asia: from 47.8% in 2000 to 77.0% in 2024. World: from 61.3% to 73.7%.
data_line: Data: WHO/UNICEF JMP via UN SDG Global Database, series SH_H2O_SAFE, extracted 1 Nov 2026
alt: Central and Southern Asia: safely managed drinking water up 29.2 points since 2000. Central and S. Asia: from 47.8% in 2000 to 77.0% in 2024. World: from 61.3% to 73.7%. Sub-Saharan Africa: 17.4% in 2000 to 31.7% in 2024; N. Africa and W. Asia: 66.5% in 2000 to 76.2% in 2024; Central and S. Asia: 47.8% in 2000 to 77.0% in 2024; E. and S.-E. Asia: 68.2% in 2000 to 75.3% in 2024; Latin America, Caribbean: 70.1% in 2000 to 78.9% in 2024; Europe and N. America: 91.9% in 2000 to 94.2% in 2024; World: 61.3% in 2000 to 73.7% in 2024
question: What lies behind the change in safely managed drinking water in Central and Southern Asia, and what could others learn from it?
